You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Calling Flush on the ETag response writer sends buffered bytes to the client before the response is complete, so the ETag can no longer be set (the request says Flush must not bypass the buffer).

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Trailers lost. Handler sets `Trailer: X-Sum`, writes "body", then sets `X-Sum: abc`. Unwrapped: trailer `X-Sum:[abc]`. Wrapped: `trailer=map[X-Sum:[]]`. The snapshot in `send` clears the trailer.
- [blocking] Hijack after Write drops the buffered response. Handler does `Write("hello")`, then `Hijack()`, then writes "RAW". Unwrapped wire: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... hello RAW`. Wrapped wire: `"RAW"`. `Hijack` sets streaming without sending the buffer.
- [blocking] Outer middleware header lost. Outer middleware sets `X-After` after `next.ServeHTTP` returns; handler writes nothing. Unwrapped `X-After="1"`, wrapped `""`. ETag commits headers in `finish` before the outer code runs.
- [blocking] Handler-set non-canonical key duplicates ETag. Handler does `w.Header()["ETag"] = {"\"mine\""}`. Wire: `ETag: "mine"` and `Etag: "2d71…"`. `finish` checks `ew.header["Etag"]` (canonical key only), so it adds a second ETag. Criterion 3 requires the handler's tag to be the only one.
- [blocking, known (b) confirmed] `WriteHeader(404)` then `Write` on a real server logs `http: superfluous response.WriteHeader call from ...(*etagResponseWriter).WriteHeader (etag.go:61)`.
- [minor] Known (a) confirmed: `Compress(5)(ETag(h))` gives a gzip 200 and an identity 200 with the same ETag (`"f7ed…"`). The doc's claim that each coding gets its own tag is false.
- [minor] Consequence of (a): an identity client sending the gzip-derived tag gets 304. Not reproduced as a wrong-content bug, but it shares one validator across codings.
- [minor] `FEATURE_FLOW.md` is an untracked file at the repo root, outside the diff. Orchestrator should decide whether it belongs.
- [minor] `etag_test.go` was not reviewed for criterion 8 (I attacked the code, not the tests).
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] 1xx after a buffered 200 is forwarded immediately, so the wire differs from bare net/http. Bare net/http ignores the superfluous 103. ETag sends it: `HTTP/1.1 103 Early Hints\r\n\r\nHTTP/1.1 200 OK...`. Cause: the 1xx case in WriteHeader precedes the `ew.header != nil` guard. Reproduced with handler `WriteHeader(200); WriteHeader(103); Write("hi")` over a real httptest server.
- [blocking] 304 does not remove representation headers set with non-canonical keys. Handler sets `w.Header()["content-type"]` and `["content-length"]`, then a matching If-None-Match. Wire: `HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified\r\nEtag: "v1"\r\ncontent-length: 5\r\ncontent-type: text/plain\r\n...`. Cause: writeNotModified uses canonical Del. Criterion 4 requires these removed.
- [minor] A panicking handler discards the buffered 200 instead of sending a truncated 200 the way bare net/http would. Not reproduced as a bug; behaviour change only, noted for the record.
- [minor] ETag wrapper does not forward io.ReaderFrom, so the sendfile fast path is lost for buffered responses. Not in the criteria; not reproduced.

GOAL: Fix round 1 for the new `middleware.ETag` in /tmp/ff-eval-d3yb2hgv/workspace (middleware/etag.go, middleware/etag_test.go; note a simplifier has since edited etag.go: the `status` field was replaced by `header != nil`). Fix each finding below and add a regression test for each in etag_test.go.

FINDINGS TO FIX:
1. Doc comment on ETag gets Compress ordering backwards. `r.Use(Compress(5)); r.Use(ETag)` makes Compress the OUTER layer, so ETag sees and hashes the UNCOMPRESSED body (gzip and identity clients get the same tag). `r.Use(ETag); r.Use(Compress(5))` makes ETag outer, hashing the compressed bytes, so each coding gets its own tag. Rewrite that paragraph accurately (state the fact plainly; recommending ETag outside Compress for distinct per-coding tags is fine).
2. Superfluous WriteHeader: after `WriteHeader(404)` (streaming, header==nil), `Write` calls `ew.WriteHeader(200)` again which forwards to the underlying writer → net/http logs "superfluous response.WriteHeader call". Fix: Write must only imply 200 when no final status has been set and not streaming (e.g. `if ew.header == nil && !ew.streaming`). Test with a recorder-like writer counting underlying WriteHeader calls.
3. Trailers dropped: handler sets `w.Header().Set("Trailer","X-Sum")`, writes body, then `w.Header().Set("X-Sum","abc")` → unwrapped the client gets trailer X-Sum=abc, wrapped it's empty because `send` clears the live header map and copies the snapshot. Fix: in `send`, before clearing, keep the live header values; after the WriteHeader+Write, copy back into the underlying header map the values for keys declared in the snapshot's `Trailer` header(s) (comma-separated, canonicalize keys) and any keys with the `http.TrailerPrefix` prefix. Test via httptest.NewServer and resp.Trailer after reading the body.
4. Hijack after a buffered Write drops the buffered 200: handler `Write("hello")`, then `Hijack()` → unwrapped, "HTTP/1.1 200 ... hello" reaches the wire before hijack; wrapped it's lost. Fix: in Hijack, if not streaming and a 200 has been buffered (header != nil), send the buffered response (no ETag) and flush the underlying writer if it's a Flusher before hijacking. If nothing was written yet, just hijack. Test over a real server with a raw TCP client or just verify via a fake underlying writer that records writes before Hijack.
5. Non-canonical ETag key duplicates: handler does `w.Header()["ETag"] = []string{"\"mine\""}` → wire carries both `ETag: "mine"` and a computed `Etag: ...`. Fix: treat the handler as having set an ETag if the snapshot has the key under any casing (check `"Etag"` and `"ETag"`, or loop with strings.EqualFold), and use that value for If-None-Match matching and in writeNotModified's Last-Modified check. Test: no second ETag added, and If-None-Match "mine" → 304.

Accepted limitation (do NOT fix): an outer middleware setting headers after next returns is lost because ETag commits the response at the end. Mention it in one short sentence in the doc comment.

CONSTRAINTS: stdlib only; touch only middleware/etag.go and middleware/etag_test.go; keep If-None-Match parsing semantics unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. `middleware.ETag` exists in middleware/etag.go with signature `func ETag(next http.Handler) http.Handler` and a doc comment explaining behavior (buffers GET/HEAD responses, strong ETag from body, 304 on If-None-Match match, recommended placement relative to Compress: the ETag reflects the bytes it sees, so placed outside Compress it hashes compressed bytes).
2. GET/HEAD, handler responds 200 (explicitly, or implicitly by Write or by writing nothing) and did not set an ETag header: middleware sets a strong ETag `"<hex or base64url digest>"` computed from the full body (same body => same ETag; different body => different ETag; only etagc characters, no `W/`), and writes the buffered body unchanged.
   Hostile: body written in many small Writes (ETag equals that of one big write); empty body on GET; HEAD where the handler writes no body (do NOT set an ETag computed from the empty body — omit it, since the HEAD representation would otherwise get the wrong ETag; a HEAD handler that does write the body gets the same ETag as GET).
3. A handler-set ETag (strong or weak `W/"..."`) is never overwritten or removed on 200 responses.
4. If-None-Match matching per RFC 9110 §13.1.2 with weak comparison: `*` matches any 200 response (even one with no ETag); a comma-separated list matches if any member weakly equals the response ETag (`W/"a"` matches `"a"` and vice versa); OWS around members allowed. On match: status 304, no body, ETag header kept (plus Cache-Control, Content-Location, Date, Expires, Vary as set by handler), and Content-Type, Content-Length, Content-Encoding removed (as net/http's FileServer writeNotModified does). On no match: the normal 200 response.
   Hostile: an entity-tag containing a comma `"a,b"` (valid etagc) must be parsed as one tag, not split; malformed members (`abc` unquoted, `"unterminated`, `W/` alone, empty string, `,,`, `W/ "x"`) must not panic and must not match — a malformed member stops/ignores parsing without producing a false match; case-sensitive opaque tags (`"ABC"` != `"abc"`); handler-set ETag that is not a valid entity-tag never yields a 304 except via `*`.
5. Methods other than GET and HEAD (POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH...) pass through unchanged and unbuffered: the original writer (or one forwarding all its capabilities) is used, no ETag added, If-None-Match ignored.
6. Non-200 responses (201, 204, 206, 301, 404, 500, and a handler that itself returns 304) on GET/HEAD pass through unchanged: same status, headers, body; no ETag added, no 304 conversion. Ideally they stream through rather than being held in the buffer once WriteHeader(non-200) is called.
   Hostile: WriteHeader called twice (second call must not change what the client sees vs. stdlib behavior / must not panic); 1xx informational WriteHeader(103) before the final 200 is forwarded immediately and does not count as the final status; Write before WriteHeader means 200.
7. Writer capabilities, matching the sibling middleware/compress.go `compressResponseWriter`: implements `Unwrap() http.ResponseWriter` (so `http.ResponseController` works), `http.Hijacker` and `http.Pusher` forwarding to the underlying writer with the same `chi/middleware: ... is unavailable on the writer` errors, and `http.Flusher`. Flush while buffering a 200 means the handler wants to stream: the middleware gives up on the ETag (omits it, never emits a wrong one, no 304), writes status + headers + buffered bytes to the underlying writer, flushes it, and passes all further writes straight through.
   Hostile: Flush called before any Write; Flush on an underlying writer that is not a Flusher (no panic); ResponseController(w).Flush() from the handler.
8. Tests in middleware/etag_test.go (package middleware) covering criteria 2-7, including the hostile inputs listed, using httptest and/or chi router like sibling tests.
9. README.md "Core middlewares" table gets an `[ETag]` row (in alphabetical position, after [CleanPath]/[ContentCharset] area — keep the table's column formatting) and a `[ETag]: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware#ETag` link line among the link definitions.
10. Standing: existing tests pass; `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` pass; `gofmt -l .` prints nothing; go.mod unchanged (stdlib only).
